Header: Michael Burry Compares OpenAI, Anthropic, SpaceX IPO Hype To Dot-Com Bubble

Header: Pentagon awards Microsoft $9.7 billion deal in bid to cut costs, end license sprawl
Content: The Pentagon has awarded Microsoft a five-year, $9.69 billion agreement to consolidate software licenses across its military branches, intelligence community, and the U.S. Coast Guard. The agreement, called the Core Enterprise Technology Agreement, centralizes purchases of Microsoft 365 subscriptions, cloud services, and on-premises licensing, leveraging the department's full purchasing power.

CISOs must strategize for managing this new AI-driven security landscape and its implications for data security and operational oversight.

Header: Cisco report finds no closed frontier AI model is safe from multi-turn attacks
Content: A new report from Cisco Systems Inc. indicates that no closed flagship large language model is safe from multi-turn attacks, with adversarial success rates significantly increasing compared to single-prompt attacks. The study, which evaluated 15 proprietary models from major AI developers, revealed that models performing well on single-turn benchmarks often failed when attackers could engage in continuous conversation. Cisco advises organizations to demand more comprehensive attack success rate data from model providers and implement robust security measures beyond the models themselves.

Header: Kali365 phishing kit bypasses MFA and steals Microsoft logins
Content: The FBI has issued a warning about "Kali365," a new phishing-as-a-service (PhaaS) platform that enables attackers to hijack Microsoft 365 accounts by stealing access tokens, bypassing multi-factor authentication (MFA). This technique exploits legitimate Microsoft URLs for device sign-in flows, tricking users into granting attackers OAuth access and refresh tokens. The stolen tokens allow attackers persistent access to Outlook, OneDrive, and Teams, enabling them to read emails, access files, and send phishing messages from compromised accounts.

This situation suggests that rate hikes may not slow the economy and inflation as expected, potentially allowing rates to climb further.
